## What was built
The API declared in `hpack_spec.mbt` is implemented across focused, single-responsibility files:
- `integer.mbt` — prefixed integers (§5.1): N-bit prefix + base-128 continuation octets, `Int64` accumulation, `2^31−1` limit, `IntegerOverflow` (value or >5 continuation octets) and `UnexpectedEof`; minimal encoding.

- `static_table.mbt` — Appendix A, 61 entries.
- `dynamic_table.mbt` — `HeaderField::size` (`name+value+32`), newest-first entries, exact size accounting, eviction on insert/oversize/size-change.
- `decoder.mbt` — all five §6 representations, combined index address space, name-copied-before-eviction, size-update placement/limit checks, every decoding-error condition.
- `encoder.mbt` — the deterministic greedy strategy (exact → indexed smallest index; name → literal with incremental indexing; else literal name+value), both string-literal forms, the two non-indexing single-field forms, and §4.2 size-update signalling (smallest requested then final).

## What I built

Layout (root `ini` package, split by concern):

- `internal.mbt` — `priv suberror IniError`, character classes (blank/comment/control), blank trimming, and physical line splitting (LF + CRLF, trailing newline doesn't create a phantom line).
- `scanner.mbt` — continuation-marker detection (odd vs even trailing backslash runs), first-separator lookup, and strict section-header parsing.
- `value.mbt` — quoted/unquoted carriers, inline-comment stripping, and per-carrier escape decoding.
- `parser.mbt` — `pub fn parse`: line classification, section tracking, entry assembly (global vs sections, last-wins, section re-open).
- `printer.mbt` — `pub fn print`: every value in a double-quoted carrier with `\\ \" \n \r \t` escaped, section names quote-wrapped, keys sorted for determinism.
- `ini_edge_test.mbt` — 79 extra black-box tests, names prefixed `seekmoon/` so they cannot collide with another suite.
- `README.md` — overview, architecture, pipeline, escape table, usage, testing, and design rationale.

## Key semantics implemented

- Sections: `[name]` with trimmed names, spaces/unicode/punctuation/inner quotes kept, one wrapping quote pair stripped (`["x"]` → `x`), nested brackets / empty names / unclosed / trailing text rejected.
- Entries: first `=` or `:` wins (`url=...`, `time: 12:30:45` preserved), key trimmed and validated (non-empty, no control chars), keys verbatim (escapes not decoded), duplicate last-wins.
- Values: quoted values close on their own physical line (so a quote can't span lines) with only blanks/comment after; unquoted values strip an inline `;`/`#` only when preceded by a blank, then trim and decode.
- Continuations: odd trailing-backslash run continues onto the next line; even run is escaped literals; marker at EOF is an error; only unquoted values continue, and joined lines contribute text (their separators/quotes/comment markers are ordinary).
- Escapes per carrier: unquoted `\n \r \t \\`; `"..."` adds `\"`; `'...'` only `\\ \'`; anything else kept verbatim.

## Key design decisions (from the spec's own grammar)

- **Continuation before escapes** — trailing-backslash runs are counted on raw bytes, giving the exact run-length table (`a\`+`b=1` → `ab=1`; `a\\` → `a\`; …).
- **Inline comments need a preceding space/tab**, so `a;b` is literal; quoted values keep markers verbatim.
- **Section syntax is strict** (`[name]` + whitespace only) while a quoted value may be followed by an optional comment — the asymmetry in the spec's formal grammar.
- **A trailing newline is not a line**, so a dangling `\` at EOF is an error with or without a final newline.
- Everything scans `StringView` code units and only copies stored keys/values.

## Key semantics

Implemented a complete, general Protocol Buffers wire-format codec in MoonBit, and validated it end to end.

## What was built
Four implementation files (root `protobuf` package) that provide every `declare`d entry point in `protobuf_spec.mbt`:

- [reader.mbt](/home/runner/work/openseek-swe-agi/openseek-swe-agi/tasks/protobuf_run_1/reader.mbt) — `ProtobufError`, the chunk-aware `fill`/`read_exact`/`skip_n` helpers, `BytesReader`, and `LimitedReader[T]` (an opaque window over another reader).
- [varint.mbt](/home/runner/work/openseek-swe-agi/openseek-swe-agi/tasks/protobuf_run_1/varint.mbt) — the single ten-byte varint decoder (non-minimal accepted, bits past the 64th dropped, 11th byte raises) plus zigzag32/64.
- [decode.mbt](/home/runner/work/openseek-swe-agi/openseek-swe-agi/tasks/protobuf_run_1/decode.mbt) — typed readers, `read_tag`, int32-bounded `read_length`, `read_bytes`/`read_string` (strict UTF-8, BOM kept), `read_packed` through a `LimitedReader`, and `read_unknown` with iterative group skipping.
- [encode.mbt](/home/runner/work/openseek-swe-agi/openseek-swe-agi/tasks/protobuf_run_1/encode.mbt) — canonical writers for every scalar, key, bytes and string.

### Key design points
- **Streaming without assuming a full buffer:** every value is reassembled by looping over partial `read`s; EOF mid-value raises.
- **Varints:** any encoding ≤10 bytes accepted (non-minimal included), tenth-byte bits beyond the 64th dropped, 11th continuation byte overflows, minimal writes.
- **32-bit readers** take the low 32 bits; `sint*` zigzag; negative `int32`/`enum` sign-extend to ten bytes.
- **Fixed-width** little-endian, float/double bit-exact via `reinterpret_*`.
- **Length prefixes** int32-bounded, and payloads are gathered in bounded chunks so an oversized prefix raises instead of allocating.
- **Strict UTF-8** via `@utf8.decode(..., ignore_bom=false)`.
- **Packed** elements decoded through a `LimitedReader` window; **groups** skipped with an explicit stack (no deep recursion).
